\chapter{Chapter03 — Query Learning}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.QueryLearning}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Chosen-input query batch]
\lean{FABL.queryInputBatchProgram}
\label{FABL.queryInputBatchProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.map, FABL.Sign}
Given $m$ inputs in the $n$-dimensional sign cube and a target accessible by membership
queries, this program queries the target at each input and returns the resulting list of
input-label pairs, in the original order.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Query batch run distribution]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_queryInputBatchProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_queryInputBatchProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningCost.toTriple_injective, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_map, FABL.queryInputBatchProgram}
\difficulty{4}
For a natural number $n$, a Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, a natural number
$m$, and specified inputs $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\{−1,1\}^n$, running the query batch program
returns the labeled sequence $(x_i,f(x_i))_{i=1}^m$ with probability one. Its cost is
$(0,m,m)$: no random examples, $m$ queries, and $m$ units of work.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Queried random-example batch]
\lean{FABL.queriedRandomExampleBatchProgram}
\label{FABL.queriedRandomExampleBatchProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.Sign, FABL.queryInputBatchProgram}
Given a natural number $m$, this program draws $m$ independent uniform inputs from the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, queries the target at each input, and returns the resulting
input-label pairs.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Queried random batch run distribution]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_queriedRandomExampleBatchProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_queriedRandomExampleBatchProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningCost.toTriple_injective, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.queriedRandomExampleBatchProgram, FABL.runWithCost_queryInputBatchProgram, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
For a natural number $n$, a Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and a natural
number $m$, the program’s run law is that of drawing a uniformly random sequence
$(x_i)_{i=1}^m$ from $\{−1,1\}^n$ and returning the labeled sequence
$(x_i,f(x_i))_{i=1}^m$. Every outcome has cost $(0,m,mn+m)$: no random examples, $m$
membership queries, and $mn+m$ units of work.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Finite family matrix index bijection]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyMatrixIndexEquiv}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyMatrixIndexEquiv}
\leanok
Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of the $n$ coordinate indices, and let
$m$ be a natural number. There is a bijection between pairs consisting of a member of
$\mathcal F$ and an index in $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, and the indices in
$\{0,\ldots,|\mathcal F|m-1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite family matrix reindexing]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyLinearToMatrixEquiv}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyLinearToMatrixEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.finiteFamilyMatrixIndexEquiv}
For a finite family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, a natural number $m$,
and a type $\alpha$, reindexing a function on $\{0,\ldots,|\mathcal F|m-1\}$ gives an
equivalent function assigning to each member of $\mathcal F$ a function on
$\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, with values in $\alpha$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fourier estimator from queried inputs]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorFromInputs}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p090-b002
}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorFromInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.bind, FABL.Sign, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorLabeledOutput, FABL.finiteFamilyLinearToMatrixEquiv, FABL.queryInputBatchProgram}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let
$m\in\mathbb{N}$, and supply $|\mathcal{F}|m$ inputs from the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^n$.
The program queries the target at these inputs, arranges the resulting labeled inputs as
a matrix indexed by $\mathcal{F}$ and $m$ samples, charges $|\mathcal{F}|m(n+1)$ local
computation steps, and returns the finite-family Fourier estimator as a sparse Fourier
hypothesis with rational coefficients.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Queried Fourier estimator output]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput, FABL.finiteFamilyLinearToMatrixEquiv}
Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family
of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $m$ be a natural number, and let
$x_1,\ldots,x_{|\mathcal F|m}\in\{−1,1\}^n$ be inputs. Arrange these inputs as $m$
inputs for each member of $\mathcal F$ using the natural reindexing, and apply the
finite-family Fourier estimator to obtain a sparse Fourier hypothesis on $n$ variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Inner cost of queried estimation]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorInnerCost}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorInnerCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningCost}
For a finite family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a natural number
$m$, the estimator's inner cost uses no random examples, charges $|\mathcal F|m$
membership queries, and charges $|\mathcal F|m+|\mathcal F|m(n+1)$ units of work.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fourier estimator with sampled inputs]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p090-b002
}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorFromInputs}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let
$m\in\mathbb{N}$. The program draws $|\mathcal{F}|m$ independent uniform inputs from the
sign cube, then runs the queried finite-family Fourier estimator on those inputs and
returns a sparse Fourier hypothesis with rational coefficients.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fourier estimator query and work cost]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorCost}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningCost}
For a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}$,
the estimator cost has zero random-example calls, $|\mathcal{F}|m$ membership queries,
and $|\mathcal{F}|mn+|\mathcal{F}|m+|\mathcal{F}|m(n+1)$ charged local computation
steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform distribution under matrix indexing]
\lean{FABL.map_uniformPMF_finiteFamilyLinearToMatrixEquiv}
\label{FABL.map_uniformPMF_finiteFamilyLinearToMatrixEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.finiteFamilyLinearToMatrixEquiv, FABL.map_uniformPMF_equiv, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, and let $m$ be a
natural number. Choose uniformly a function from $\\{1,\\ldots,|\\mathcal F|m\\}$ to the
Boolean cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$, then reindex its values as a function on $\\mathcal
F\\times\\{1,\\ldots,m\\}$. The resulting distribution is uniform on the functions from
$\\mathcal F$ to the set of functions from $\\{1,\\ldots,m\\}$ to $\\{-1,1\\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Confidence allocation across a finite family]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidenceForTotal}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidenceForTotal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveLearningParameter}
Let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$\delta$ be rational with $0<\delta\leq 1/2$. The confidence parameter assigned to each
member of the family is $\delta/|\mathcal F|$, which also lies in $(0,1/2]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Samples per Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientAccuracy, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidenceForTotal, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq\tfrac12$ and
$0<\delta\leq\tfrac12$. The number of samples per coefficient is the Fourier-estimator
sample count at the family’s coefficient accuracy for $\varepsilon$ and its confidence
allocation for total failure parameter $\delta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fourier estimator with confidence parameters]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p090-b002
}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq\tfrac12$ and
$0<\delta\leq\tfrac12$. The program draws the number of independent uniform sign-cube
inputs prescribed per coefficient by the family’s accuracy and confidence parameters,
then runs the queried finite-family Fourier estimator on them and returns a sparse
Fourier hypothesis with rational coefficients.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube, let $\\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite
family of coordinate subsets, and let $0<\\varepsilon,\\delta\\le 1/2$. For each
$S\\in\\mathcal F$, take the prescribed number of inputs and estimate its Fourier
coefficient by the empirical average of $f(x)\\prod_{i\\in S}x_i$. If the Fourier weight
of $f$ outside $\\mathcal F$ is at most $\\varepsilon/2$, and every estimated
coefficient differs from its true coefficient by strictly less than
$\\varepsilon/(2|\\mathcal F|)$, then the sign of the estimated Fourier sum has relative
Hamming distance at most $\\varepsilon$ from $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Failure probability of the Fourier estimator]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_failureProbability_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b006
}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_failureProbability_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn, FABL.LearningProgram.eventProbability, FABL.LearningProgram.eventProbability_eq_toMeasure_real_of_runWithCost_eq_map, FABL.LearningProgram.randomExampleMatrixInputLaw, FABL.LearningProgram.randomExampleMatrixInputLaw_eq_uniformPMF, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.evaluate, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput, FABL.measure_queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_failure_le, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorCost, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.runWithCost_queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples_uniformMatrix, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $\mathcal F$ be a
nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2]$. Suppose the total squared Fourier weight of $f$ outside
$\mathcal F$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$. Then the probability that the estimator with
parameters $\mathcal F,\varepsilon,\delta$ outputs a hypothesis whose relative Hamming
distance from $f$ is strictly greater than $\varepsilon$ is at most $\delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact cost of the Fourier estimator]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_cost_eq}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_cost_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorCost, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.runWithCost_queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and
let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For
accuracy and confidence parameters $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2]$, every outcome in the
support of the estimator's run-with-cost distribution has cost $(0,\,|\mathcal
F|m,\,|\mathcal F|mn+|\mathcal F|m+|\mathcal F|m(n+1))$, where $m$ is the estimator's
prescribed sample count per family member.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact query count for Fourier estimation]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_queries_eq}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_queries_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_cost_eq, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. Every possible
outcome of the confidence-parameter finite-family Fourier estimator uses exactly
$|\mathcal F|M$ membership queries, where $M$ is the number of samples used per
coefficient at accuracy parameter $\varepsilon$ and total confidence parameter $\delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact local work of Fourier estimation]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_work_eq}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_work_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_cost_eq, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. Every possible
outcome of the confidence-parameter finite-family Fourier estimator has charged local
work exactly $|\mathcal F|Mn+|\mathcal F|M+|\mathcal F|M(n+1)$, where $M$ is the number
of samples used per coefficient at accuracy parameter $\varepsilon$ and total confidence
parameter $\delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sample count bound per coefficient]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient_cast_le}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientAccuracy, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidenceForTotal, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount_cast_le, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of
subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy
$0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. If $M$ is the sample count per coefficient chosen for
accuracy $\varepsilon$ and total confidence $\delta$, then, viewed as a rational number,
$M\le 16|\mathcal F|^2L/\varepsilon^2$, where $L$ is the failure-bit count associated
with confidence parameter $\delta/|\mathcal F|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query complexity bound for Fourier estimation]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_queries_cast_le}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_queries_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidenceForTotal, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_queries_eq, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient_cast_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. For any possible
outcome of the confidence-parameter finite-family Fourier estimator, the number $q$ of
membership queries, viewed as a rational number, satisfies $q\le 16|\mathcal F|^3
L/\varepsilon^2$, where $L$ is the failure-bit count associated with confidence
parameter $\delta/|\mathcal F|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Local work bound for Fourier estimation]
\lean{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_work_cast_le}
\label{FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_work_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidenceForTotal, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithConfidence_work_eq, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.queriedFiniteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient_cast_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. For any possible
outcome of the confidence-parameter finite-family Fourier estimator, its charged local
work $w$, viewed as a rational number, satisfies $w\le 32|\mathcal
